Subject: Order Form redlines / invoicing & tax questions

Hi Olga —

Thanks for the draft Order Form. We ran this by Procurement and Tax and have a few redlines and clarifying asks before we can circulate internally for PO sign-off. The redline PDF is attached. High level: 

- Invoice entity and remit: Procurement needs confirmation which Redwood legal entity will appear on the invoice for US payments. Our AP needs a consistent remit entity for ACH.
- Net terms: We usually negotiate Net 45 for platform contracts; your Order Form currently says Net 30. Will Redwood accept Net 45?
- Minimum commit / proration: We have an internal policy that requires the invoice schedule to align with quarter boundaries; can you confirm how minimum commit proration will be handled if we activate mid-quarter?
- Withholding / VAT: Our tax team noted language re: withholding tax; they want Redwood to accept customer withholding where local law applies and provide a gross-up clause only in rare cases.
- PO requirement: We require a formal PO number on all invoices. Please confirm Redwood can accept a PO on the order form and cite the field that will appear on the invoice.

Can you please loop in legal and finance so we can close these items this week? We can do a short call tomorrow 9–10am PT if that helps.

Attachments: CommonBank_OrderForm_v3_redlines.pdf

Best,
Elena
Senior Sourcing Manager, CommonBank

- Withholding: Kimberly — please advise on whether we accept customer withholding and when Redwood will require gross-up / tax indemnity.

Olga / team — see inline summary of our position and suggested contract language. I also attached a short doc with redline snippets for the MSA/Order Form.

Summary positions (commercial/legal risk view):
- Net terms: We can reasonably agree to Net 45 for this committed multi-quarter deal (DEAL-5342). Net 60 is where we start to push back for cashflow impact. If we accept Net 45 we should: a) include a 1.5% monthly late fee cap and b) reserve right to require prepayment on renewal if payment behavior deteriorates.
- Invoice entity: Acceptable to indicate Redwood Inference, Inc. as default remit entity. If CommonBank requires payments to an alternate Redwood entity, require the customer to provide W-9 / tax form for that entity and accept that this may trigger different VAT/withholding treatment.
- Withholding/gross-up: We do not accept open-ended gross-up obligations. Suggested clause: "If Customer is required by applicable law to withhold any amounts from payments to Redwood, Customer will timely withhold and remit such amounts to the relevant authority and provide Redwood with official documentation of payment; Redwood will provide a tax credit or invoice adjustment where legally required. Except to the extent Redwood has agreed in writing in advance, Customer shall not be required to gross-up payments."
- PO on invoice: Operationally fine — Finance will add a PO reference field on the PDF invoice and our AP team will accept PO numbers. Markus to confirm exact layout and confirm that PO on invoice does not change remittance entity.

Proposed redline snippet for Order Form (to propose to CommonBank):
"Payment Terms: Customer shall pay invoices within forty-five (45) days of receipt. Invoices will be issued monthly in arrears per the invoice schedule attached as Exhibit A. All invoices will reference Customer Purchase Order numbers where provided. Redwood invoices shall be issued in the name of 'Redwood Inference, Inc.' unless otherwise agreed in writing and supported by appropriate tax documentation.

Taxes and Withholding: Customer is responsible for taxes imposed on its payments except for taxes based on Redwood's net income. If Customer is required by applicable law to withhold any amount from a payment to Redwood, Customer shall withhold such amounts, remit them to the appropriate tax authority and provide Redwood with official receipts. Where withholding reduces the net amount payable to Redwood, the Parties will cooperate in good faith to determine any further adjustment required by law; Redwood will not require Customer to gross-up payments except where explicitly agreed in writing.

Proration: Fees for the initial billing period will be prorated to the effective date of Service and align with calendar quarter boundaries per Customer request: if the Service starts between the first and last day of a calendar quarter, the invoice for that quarter will reflect prorated usage through the quarter end, unless otherwise agreed in writing."

Next steps (short):
- Markus: confirm sample invoice with PO field and remit entity (send by EOD).
- Ben: confirm commercial OK for Net 45 tradeoff and any concession to minimum commit price.
- Olga: share redline PDF and set time for tomorrow call if Elena confirms.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Thanks — that plan looks good. We can confirm the 09:00–09:30 PT call tomorrow (I’ll send the calendar invite in a minute). A few quick replies before the call so the team comes prepared: 

- Net 45 is acceptable to our Finance team provided the 1.5% monthly late fee is removed — we have internal policy not to accept late-fees that could be interpreted as penalties. If Redwood needs stronger protections for receivables, we can discuss narrow credit hold rights tied to sustained late payment (e.g., 2 consecutive late payments).
- Remit entity: OK to show "Redwood Inference, Inc." on invoices. Please attach a sample invoice with the PO field and remit details (Markus).
- Proration: Confirmed — CommonBank prefers proration to align to quarter boundaries; on the call we’ll share the procurement cutover calendar that drives PO approvals.
- Withholding: Our tax team will accept the suggested withholding language (no open-ended gross-up) but will ask Redwood to provide timely tax receipts when withholding applies.

Also, two operational asks for the final Order Form: 1) a separate line in the invoice for activation/one-time fees (if any) so they map to accounting codes; 2) an explicit field for Customer Billing Contact on the Order Form.

I’ve sent the calendar invite for 09:00 PT tomorrow and attached our internal procurement checklist; please review before the call.

Best,
Elena
Senior Sourcing Manager, CommonBank
